countable.description: The pagehide listener commits through request(), which takes no options, so the DELETE goes out without keepalive. The snackbar guide says to commit on pagehide with fetch(url, { method: 'DELETE', keepalive: true }). A request started while the page unloads is normally cancelled, so the row is gone on screen and comes back on the next visit. The stand-in is a timer that never fires once the page is gone.

The save handler wraps request() in try/finally with no catch. A rejected request (a network error, which a real fetch gives and the stand-in never does) resets the button and escapes as an unhandled rejection, and the failure snackbar never shows. The person sees the dialog return to Save address with no error.

A save that resolves with ok false shows its error snackbar while the modal dialog is open. Snackbar appends its container to document.body, under the modal dialog's backdrop, so the error is dimmed and away from the form. Chromium, with the POST stand-in forced to ok false, showed the bar blurred under the backdrop. The stand-in POST always resolves ok, so only a real failure reaches this path. This is the framework-stage destructive-list run 2 count.
